title: LOTR Fans Need To “Be Patient,” Kingdom Come Dev Says About New Middle-earth RPG
description: Kingdom Come developer Warhorse is working on multiple new games, including a The Lord of the Rings role-playing game. We don't know much about it right now, and Warhorse isn't likely to share more details anytime soon. In a post on social media, Warhorse said, "We're excited to tell you guys more, you've just gotta be patient for now." In short, you should be more like an Ent and slow down. Good things come to those who wait, after all. Warhorse announced the game earlier this year, saying it will be a "deeply immersive" open-world Middle-earth RPG. A scene from 2002's The Two Towers.The game will feature a “living world” populated by “interesting characters, memorable places, and, of course, a strong narrative focus," the developers said. This doesn't tell us much about it, but it’s a starting point for understanding where the game may be headed. We also know that Deliverance 2 design director Viktor Bocan is leading the development of the untitled Lord of the Rings game. In addition to the new Lord of the Rings game, Warhorse is producing a new Kingdom Come game, along with a Kingdom Come movie. As for the Lord of the Rings game series, Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is said to be working on its own game as well. Both Crystal Dynamics and Warhorse are owned by Embracer, which controls the rights to The Lord of the Rings. Beyond these games, Aspyr Media has teased more re-releases of classic The Lord of the Rings games following the shadow-drop of War in the North. The Lord of the Rings series remains popular outside of games, too. Prime Video’s The Rings of Power series returns for a third season this November and Andy Serkis is directing The Hunt for Gollum, which will be out in 2027.

title: GTA 6 Has A Point Of No Return For Players Who Take Crime Too Far
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is looking to add some extra wrinkles to several of its established gameplay pillars, but the biggest update here might just be the inclusion of an honor system. Taking a page from Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 will remind you that actions have consequences, as your less-than-legal activities will feed into a criminal profile that evolves with you. Not only are there various profiles within this that gauge just how effective you are at crime--or bloodthirsty--but developer Rockstar Games will let you break it entirely if you cause too much chaos. "There's no right or wrong way to play the game," GTA 6 co-head of development Rob Nelson said to YouTuber TGG. "Just a bit more choice now. How do you want to play this game if your actions may have some impact on things? You can still cause as much chaos as you want if that's what you want to do. I don't think it changes what GTA is. It changes what it can be for people who want to engage with it in that way. You still have as much freedom as you had before; you can just do more now, and you have more choice in terms of how you approach situations." https://youtu.be/33t4kUEBL5k At the highest level, players can have a criminal record that labels them as a "Professional," and from there, the states descend into Aggressive, Violent, and Psycho. Reaching the fifth, currently unnamed state, is said to be particularly tough, but once you do, there's no return from a full descent into villainy. The idea is that players will have the freedom to alternate between criminal profiles or replay the game while aiming to align with those particular states. Players can also disable notifications about their profile status changing, and the co-protagonists Jason and Lucia will each have their own profile that changes throughout the course of the game depending on the actions you take with them. How these states ultimately influence the story of GTA 6 has yet to be revealed, but we'd wager that being a homicidal loose cannon probably won't end well by the time that the end credits roll. GTA 6 will include several other features designed to heighten the game's sense of realism. Non-playable characters will notice if you're carrying weapons out in public, cars require more finesse to steal, and yes, you can throw dog poop at people. At the same time, Rockstar has also removed one of the worst legacy features from GTA 6, as you'll no longer need to wear your thumb out when you're outrunning cops by mashing a single button. title: Witcher 4 Dev “Not Worried” About Future Of Consoles Despite Rising Costs
description: CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski is "not worried" about the future of consoles, despite rising costs that could impact growth in the sector. Speaking to The Game Business, Nowakowski said consoles continue to be "necessary to broaden the audience" for casual and semi-casual players. "It’s important to have easy to plug in and enjoy gaming," he said. He said consoles will "weather the storm" they are currently facing today, including pricing. Nowakowski also said he's heard the rumors that the PS6 and next Xbox could be delayed, but he said, "I don't know if they're true." A scene from The Witcher 4.Generally speaking, Nowakowski said CD Projekt doesn't spend too much time worrying about how the company reaches people. "Content is the king. And if the content is right, people will find a way to play it," the executive said. The developers at CD Projekt would ask for "as much power" as possible to help display games in the best possible light. However, Nowakowski said the developers at CD Projekt are "realistic," too, so if next-gen consoles get delayed, some ideas that would require new, more powerful hardware might get "put on a shelf for the future." "We’d have to adjust. We’re not worried on the commercial side. Consoles are here to stay," he said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s CD Projekt has multiple games in the works that are likely planned for new consoles, as The Witcher 4 is lined up for release in 2028, with Cyberpunk 2 likely coming sometime after. Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have raised hardware prices due to global market factors, including tariffs and the AI-fueled demand for components and memory. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma recently said it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use cases outside of gaming, even if it means that Xbox consoles are now more expensive than ever. Nintendo, for its part, has received refunds for President Trump's tariffs--which were deemed illegal--but said it has no legal requirement to pass along any money to consumers who paid more. Sony, meanwhile, has received gigantic tariff refunds as well, with no plans to pass anything along. There are rumors that the next wave of new consoles could cost $1,000 or more, and that could have a dramatic, negative effect on the market overall.

title: Sony Warns PlayStation Customers Against Harassing Support Staff Amid Disc Backlash
description: Sony's decision to kill off PlayStation game discs has been met with almost universal disdain since it was first announced, and it looks like its employees have been caught in the crossfire. Just about every Sony announcement or social media post is met with calls for it to reverse its decision, and Sony Japan has instituted a new anti-harassment policy to protect the customer service employees who have had to deal with a vocal contingent of dissatisfied consumers. These changes also align with new workplace laws in Japan that will take effect later this year. "Similar to other companies in Japan, Sony Interactive Entertainment has published its policy in compliance with a new law taking effect on October 1, which requires employers in Japan to implement measures to address customer harassment," Sony said in response to GameSpot. According to the policy, Sony will restrict people who "exceed what is considered reasonable" when interacting with customer service, including "unreasonable demands" for compensation or apologies. Abusive language, threats, and "forcing someone to prostrate themselves" can also get you cut off from the help desk, as will visiting offices or related facilities without permission. Sony added that it will work with the police and lawyers, if necessary, to protect its employees. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s&pp=0gcJCRoMAYcqIYzv While customer service workers are currently dealing with backlash over Sony's decision to focus on an all-digital future, the company has also been criticized for several more recent actions. Sony responded to a class action lawsuit in which it was accused of not clearly informing consumers that its digital store sells game licenses, not full games. Various publishers have also accused Sony of anti-competitive moves and of working toward creating a monopoly through its digital storefront. Sony will pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement over digital game prices. Even with all of that bad press, the company is still moving "cautiously forward" with its plan to end game disc production, as no amount of negative comments or week-long boycotts has convinced Sony to change its mind. Expect a flood of comments highlighting this during this week's back-to-back State of Play livestreams.

title: Square Enix Shares Jumped On Buyout Rumors, But The Company Says It’s Not Happening
description: Following a report that Square Enix was potentially exploring going private, the company behind hit franchises like Final Fantasy has released a statement denying the claims. Japanese business magazine Sentaku originally reported that Square Enix was exploring this possibility and that foreign investment funds were rumored to be interested in a deal, which saw Square Enix's stock rise by 7%. "The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix. (the Company) going private," Square Enix wrote in a press release. "However, this information was not announced by the Company. No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private." Even if Square Enix were to change its mind, buying back all shares wouldn't be cheap. Depending on daily stock fluctuations on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Square Enix has a Market Capitalization of roughly $6.67 billion to $6.82 billion. While that's pretty big, Square Enix still pales in comparison to the market valuations of its fellow Japanese gaming giants, Nintendo ($64 billion) and Capcom ($11.33 billion). Where the company stands out is that it has a stable revenue base, and recent financial overhauls have improved its capital efficiency. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3NrZKxdh6Q Square Enix is also more than just a video game developer and publisher, as it also publishes manga magazines and graphic novels under its Gangan Comics imprint, operates arcade franchises under the Taito Corporation banner, and it has a massive merchandising arm. Looking ahead, Square Enix has plenty of games in the pipeline, including the upcoming releases of Final Fantasy Resonance and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation. That would make it a lucrative prospect for an offer to go private, as seen in the case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund--alongside Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner’s private equity firm Affinity Partners and investment company Silver Lake--taking ownership of Electronic Arts last month, concluding a $55 billion deal. Unfortunately, this takeover has left EA saddled with billions in debt, and it's feared that mass layoffs will follow as the company aims to cut costs.

Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
description: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement (via IGN) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible for a payment. The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024, alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store." Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed. You are potentially eligible for a payout if you purchased one of the affected games via the PlayStation Store between April 1, 2019 and December 31, 2023. Dozens of games are listed in the official court documents, including Nier: Automata, Resident Evil 4, The Last of Us Remastered, and Vita games like Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Killzone: Mercenary.

title: GTA 6’s Extended Look Trailer Seemingly Paid Off For Netflix With Massive Viewership
description: Netflix has confirmed that GTA 6's recent "extended look" trailer was the streamer's most-viewed title overall last week, drawing 31.1 million views. The trailer was labeled an "English-language film" by Netflix, and it was No. 1 by that designation in 87 of 93 regions globally that Netflix's tracks (via Variety). The GTA 6 trailer was well ahead of the No. 2 title last week, which was the movie The Whisper Man, which had 23.2 million viewers. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpPpqZwUwl0 Netflix's view counts cover views for each title from Monday to Sunday of the previous week. A "view" is defined by Netflix as the total hours viewed divided by the total runtime. Netflix publishes this data each Tuesday. The extended look trailer was published first on Netflix before being released on Rockstar's own YouTube channel and elsewhere six hours later. Rockstar's own video has 17 million views, but YouTube counts views differently, and that represents just one channel, as numerous other sites and sources hosted it, including here at GameSpot. Netflix called its partnership with Rockstar Games for the trailer a "first-of-its-kind" offering for the popular streaming platform. Netflix's stock price has crashed since its bailed out of its deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery, and the company has undertaken numerous efforts to increase engagement and total watching time on the platform. Beyond this partnership for the GTA 6 trailer, Netflix has expanded into video podcasts. The New York Times recently reported that Netflix is in discussions to add Fox One and Peacock to the platform, while it's also been reported that Netflix could add free ad-supported TV content. As for GTA 6, the game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: The Witcher Remake Is Waiting On The Witcher 4 To Continue Development
description: CD Projekt has confirmed to GameSpot that The Witcher Remake from Fool’s Theory is currently on the back burner as the studio works on The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt’s Songs of the Past expansion and assists with the development of The Witcher 4. GameSpot reached out to CD Projekt for comment on the state of The Witcher’s remake and received the following response: "Fool's Theory team is focused mainly on the development of Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, while a relatively small part of their team is supporting the development of The Witcher 4. As we have previously announced, the development on The Witcher Remake has been temporarily integrated with The Witcher 4 due to production process dependencies. As The Witcher Remake will be built on the foundation laid by The Witcher 4, we need to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for efficient development." We first noticed something was up with The Witcher Remake when joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski mentioned roadblocks for the project in an interview with The Game Business. “We started a collaboration with Fool’s Theory. They were supposed to work on The Witcher 1 [remake], but we realized that needed a bit more time because of certain technology dependencies with The Witcher 4,” Nowakowski revealed. CD Projekt at large is transitioning from using its proprietary RED Engine for all its games to Unreal Engine. The Witcher 4 will set the standard for what a Witcher game in Unreal Engine looks like, and it appears that The Witcher 1’s remake (announced in 2022) got caught up in that technology shift. Now, Fool’s Theory is the primary developer of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt’s upcoming Songs of the Past expansion, which was unveiled at Gamescom, and is helping create The Witcher 4. Once those are complete, work on The Witcher Remake can ramp up again. This is the only image related to The Witcher's remake that CD Projekt ever publicly shared.Previous statements Nowakowski made in conversations with investors support his latest comments to The Game Business and GameSpot. In its Q3 2024 earnings report Q&A, Nowakowski said that “work is progressing” on the remake, but in the Q&A reflecting on the entire 2024 fiscal year, Nowakowski’s tone on the project changed. He explained that the remake’s development had been integrated with The Witcher 4’s. “Due to production process dependencies - among others related to assets and technology - we have decided to temporarily integrate its development with ongoing work on The Witcher 4,” he said. “As a result, a small portion of The Fool's Theory team is currently supporting The Witcher 4 team. Our goal is to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for more efficient development of The Witcher Remake.” In a Q3 2025 earnings call Q&A, Nowakowski reiterated this by stating, “the majority of the team is currently involved in the other project [Songs of the Past], and also support for The Witcher 4, so there is some limited team working on TW1, but since it’s very much tied with TW4 development…for TW1 per se, it’s a smaller group of people.” The Witcher 1’s remake does not have a release window at this time, but from Nowakowski's comments, it seems likely it won’t arrive until after The Witcher 3 Remastered later this month, Songs of the Past in 2027, and The Witcher 4 in 2028.

title: Denny’s rival dining chain files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
